Download sequences from NCBI GenBank

Source: R/ncbi.R
download_ncbi_sequences.Rd

Downloads all NCBI Nucleotide records that match a search term (written exactly as you would type it on the NCBI website) to a FASTA file, in batches. Requires an internet connection and the suggested package rentrez.

Usage

download_ncbi_sequences(
  term,
  file,
  batch_size = 500,
  max_records = Inf,
  resume = FALSE,
  api_key = Sys.getenv("ENTREZ_KEY"),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

term

NCBI Nucleotide search term, e.g. `'(ITS2) AND Embryophyta[Organism] AND ("0"[SLEN] : "10000"[SLEN])'`.

file

Output FASTA file.

batch_size

Records per request (max 10000). Default 500.

max_records

Maximum number of records to download. Default: all.

resume

If `TRUE` and `file` exists, continue an interrupted download by appending to it. If `FALSE` (default) an existing file is an error.

api_key

Optional NCBI API key. Defaults to the `ENTREZ_KEY` environment variable.

verbose

Print progress. Default `TRUE`.

Value

The number of records in `file`, invisibly.

Details

Large downloads can take a long time. If a download is interrupted, run the same command again with `resume = TRUE` to continue where it stopped. An NCBI API key (free, see <https://account.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/>) makes downloads faster.

See also

[build_reference_db()]

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("rentrez", quietly = TRUE)) {
  out <- tempfile(fileext = ".fasta")
  try(download_ncbi_sequences("Malus[Organism] AND ITS2", out, max_records = 20))
}
#> NCBI search found 399 record(s); downloading 20
#>   20 / 20
# }
